review.tagline: Next.js-native headless CMS and app framework with a React admin panel
review.summary: Payload installs into an existing Next.js /app folder and provides a TypeScript headless CMS with auth, versions and drafts, localization, and a customizable React admin. Server components can query the database directly without REST or GraphQL. The README lists website and ecommerce templates plus one-click deploys to Vercel (Neon, Vercel Blob) and Cloudflare (Workers, R2, D1).
review.audience: Next.js developers who need a self-hosted CMS or content backend
strengths: Installs inside an existing Next.js /app folder, so frontend and backend share one codebase
Auth, versions and drafts, localization, and field-level access control are built in
Generates TypeScript types for your data; hooks exist at document and field level
One-click deploy to Vercel (Neon, Blob) or Cloudflare (Workers, R2, D1)
weaknesses: README does not mention built-in AI features; it is a general CMS
Tied to Next.js and TypeScript for its native setup
Supported databases and minimum resources are not stated in the README
v2 to v3 required a migration guide, so older projects need upgrade work
needs: Needs Next.js, Database (Neon Postgres or Cloudflare D1 in one-click deploys)
